title: Investigate observability blindspots: async-retry traces + sampling misconfigurations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a capacity/regression event on 2026-03-08 we observed prolonged tail latency for Console background workflows (tenant syncs and usage rollups). Initial investigation showed retries from an async worker queue were causing transient backpressure on Redis and the runtime ingress path. Two blindspots in our observability made the impact harder to detect and remediate quickly: (1) sampled traces for async workers were set to a static low sampling rate and excluded retry spans, so causal chains into the request ingress surface were missing; (2) dashboards aggregated percentiles incorrectly (using rate-weighted means) which hid multi-modal latency behavior and late retries.

Context and why this matters: the Console is the primary product surface for customers to view cost/latency breakdowns; outages or regressions there reduce customer confidence and block ops from diagnosing SLO regressions. The specific issue caused a high-severity page for the on-call team and several customer support tickets about delayed rollups.

What we discovered:
- Trace sampling: async worker service (console-workers) sampling was globally set to 0.5% for production to control storage costs. We found a hard-coded exclusion that stripped retry-related spans (retry.*) before they were sampled, so retries were invisible in traces.
- Dashboard aggregation: the Console ingress latency dashboard used a single 'avg' and 'p95' metric computed from per-shard summaries on ingestion. Because retries produce a small number of high-latency events, the aggregation method underweights those outliers for p99+. We lacked a heatmap/percentile distribution chart for per-tenant tail behavior.
- Missing queue depth metrics: the async queue implementation emits only processed/success counters and a single gauge for 'pending_jobs_total' at coarse intervals (1m). We need higher fidelity and per-route queue depth histograms to detect short spikes.
- Alerting gaps: existing alerts were set on aggregate p95 and error-rate and therefore didn't fire early when retry spikes started. No alert existed for sudden divergence between per-route p50 and p99.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Increased trace sampling to 1% and removed the retry span exclusion locally in the staging fleet; instrumented a temporary sampling rule for retry.* spans in prod to 2% for the next 72 hours (change deployed 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC). This surfaced causal traces linking async retries -> ingress queues.
- Added an emergency Grafana dashboard (temp) showing per-tenant p50/p95/p99 from raw samples for the top 100 tenants by requests. Deployed and shared with SRE and Console PMs.
- Tuned retry backoff for console-workers to flatten momentary retry storms while we implement better mitigations.

Action items (owners + acceptance criteria):
1) Restore and extend tracing fidelity for async workflows (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate 3):
   - Add deterministic span names for retry attempts (retry.attempt, retry.backoff) and ensure they are included in sampling decision.
   - Implement a sampling policy: 0.5% default, 2% for retry.* spans, and 10% for tenants with >1% error uplift for 15m windows.
   - Acceptance: retried requests appear end-to-end in traces in prod within 10 minutes of active changes; validate with synthetic retry generator. (Target release: console-2026.03)

2) Improve queue telemetry granularity (owner: Priya Kapoor, estimate 3):
   - Emit per-route queue depth gauges at 5s cadence and histogram of job latencies for the last 5 minutes.
   - Add aggregated 'retry-spike' counter for jobs that exceed N attempts within M seconds.
   - Acceptance: dashboard shows per-route queue depth spikes with 5s resolution during a controlled load test; alert fires on >X spike.

3) Rework dashboard aggregations and add distribution views (owner: DataViz team / Emma Rodriguez, estimate 5):
   - Replace current p99 derivation with raw-percentile ingestion path for token-level latency metrics.
   - Add per-tenant latency heatmaps and a 'distribution delta' chart (p50 vs p99 divergence) for top tenants.
   - Acceptance: new dashboard surfaces the previously hidden retry spikes in a replay of the 2026-03-08 incident within 24 hours of deployment.

4) Alerting and on-call runbook updates (owner: SRE - Marcus Lee, estimate 2):
   - Add alerts for p99 > baseline * 3 for any tenant and an alert for p99/p50 ratio > 4.
   - Publish a short runbook with steps to flip the temporary sampling rule, throttle retry backoff, and identify affected tenants.
   - Acceptance: playbook reviewed by SRE and Console PM; simulated alert triggered in staging and runbook exercised.

5) Longer-term kernel: evaluate adaptive sampling by workload (owner: Applied ML/Telemetry - Ravi Patel, estimate 8):
   - Prototype an ML-based sampler that prioritize traces with anomalous retry/backpressure signals.
   - Acceptance: prototype reduces storage cost vs full sampling while increasing visibility of problematic traces in 2-week A/B test.

Follow-ups/notes:
- Links: incident postmortem doc (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/console-retry-spike-2026-03-08 (placeholder), emergency PR with sampling tweak: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1214 (placeholder), temp dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console/retry-spike-temp (placeholder).
- Risk/tradeoffs: increasing sampling will raise backend storage and query costs; we'll mitigate using targeted sampling rules rather than blanket increases. Per-route high-resolution metrics increase cardinality — we need to cap cardinality by limiting to top N tenants and sampling others.
- Decision log: we chose to avoid a full rollback and instead implement temporary targeted sampling + backoff tuning to keep visibility while minimizing cost impact.

Current blockers:
- Need ownership sign-off for production sampling policy from Observability and Privacy teams (privacy wants to ensure no sensitive PII is captured in retry spans). (blocker assigned to Liam)
- A minor migration required in metrics ingestion service to support raw-percentile ingestion path (ticket ENG-97001) — dependent.

Next steps (this week):
- Liam to land tracing span/name change and prod sampling rule by 2026-03-15.
- Priya to emit higher-fidelity queue metrics and run a load test by 2026-03-18.
- Emma to roll the new dashboard into console-2026.03 alpha by 2026-03-20.

Expected customer impact reduction: high once complete (faster RCA and fewer customer escalations).
